$comment: The reviewed half of the desktop licence notice: everything a dependency walk
cannot see. generate-third-party-notices.mjs reads this file, folds it into
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES, and fails when an entry drifts from what is installed.
See README.md in this directory for how to edit it and what is still open.

platformNative.name: @img/sharp-darwin-arm64
note: sharp's native addon for macOS arm64. electron-builder ships and unpacks the
whole @img tree (asarUnpack) because the addon cannot load from inside an asar.
Pinned here rather than read from node_modules because the package installs on
darwin/arm64 only, and the notice has to render the same on every host.

platformNative.name: @img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64
note: The prebuilt libvips-cpp dylib sharp's addon loads, shipped and unpacked with it.
The package publishes no licence file; the text below is its README's own
licensing notice, reproduced verbatim, listing every library inside the binary
and the terms each is used under. Bundled library versions are in the package's
versions.json. The LGPL entries in that table are declarations, not a compliance
conclusion — see section 10 and notices/README.md.

platformNative.name: @vscode/ripgrep-darwin-arm64
note: The `rg` executable find-across-files spawns (VC-193), shipped unpacked because
an executable cannot be spawned from inside an asar. Pinned for the same
platform reason as the two @img packages above.

toolchain.name: electron
note: The application bundle IS an Electron app: its runtime, helpers and framework
are the shipped executable, so Electron's own licence belongs here even though
the package is a devDependency. Chromium's bundled third-party licences are a
separate document that electron-builder does not copy out of the Electron
distribution — see notices/README.md, which records that as open.

toolchain.name: tailwindcss
note: A build-time dependency whose own CSS (preflight and the utility bodies it
generates) is emitted into the renderer bundle's stylesheet.

toolchain.name: tw-animate-css
note: Imported by src/renderer/src/globals.css, so its animation utilities are part of
the same emitted stylesheet.

vendored.title: shadcn/ui component primitives
vendored.evidence: apps/desktop/components.json (schema ui.shadcn.com, style new-york) and the shadcn references in the primitives themselves; the components are generated into the repository rather than installed.

vendored.title: pi-automode path canonicalization and shell lexer
vendored.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/authority/vendor/README.md pins the upstream repository, revision and tag, and lists file-by-file what was taken and what diverges. The licence text is upstream's LICENSE.md at that revision.

vendored.title: APCA-W3 lightness-contrast formulation in @volli/shared
vendored.upstream: https://github.com/Myndex/apca-w3 (apca-w3 0.1.9, a devDependency of @volli/shared used only by its tests)
vendored.evidence: The module's own comments: @volli/shared carries no runtime dependencies, so the contrast math is hand-written, and its APCA constants are described there as 'APCA-W3 0.1.9 constants (the W3C-licensed sRGBcalc formulation)' and pinned against the apca-w3 package by test.
vendored.unresolved: Known: the shipped code is written in this repository, not copied, and the apca-w3 package itself is a devDependency that never reaches the bundle; what the shipped file reproduces is the published APCA-W3 constant set and formulation. Not resolved here: whether that reproduction carries any attribution or licence obligation of its own. That is a judgement about a published algorithm rather than a packaging fact, so this entry records it and asserts nothing; it is carried in notices/README.md as an open item for the separate licensing review.

vendored.title: AI Elements chat primitives
vendored.evidence: The directory name, and docs/plans/attachments.md calling prompt-input.tsx vendored. The commit that introduced the files (02a2442) records no origin.
vendored.unresolved: Known: these files were copied in rather than written here, and the naming follows the AI Elements component registry. Not recorded anywhere in this repository: which upstream project and revision they came from, and under which licence. Nothing is asserted for them here and no licence text is reproduced. To close this, confirm the upstream project and revision, add them with the licence text to this registry, and regenerate. Until then the entry stands as an open item in notices/README.md.
